checks: The feasible set contains the vector with a_0=−1, a_1=1 and all other coordinates zero, including d=1. Coupling proves almost sure convergence; the independent fixed phase −E_0 rules out a zero atom in every limit, so the indicators converge almost surely and bounded convergence gives continuity.

Under the contradiction hypothesis there are at least two positive phases and one negative phase. All nonzero free-coordinate pairs admit two-sided sum-preserving variations with a_0 fixed, so their partial derivatives agree and are positive. Conditioning the added positive or negative phase gives the stated transform on the correct half-line.

The supporting tangent to log f at zero bounds f by f(0) on the nonpositive half-line if the tangent slope is nonnegative, and on the nonnegative half-line if the slope is nonpositive. Integrability and continuity force strict inequality on a nonempty interval of the chosen half-line. Since one free coefficient of each sign is available, the relevant transform gives the common value 0<q<1 even when the tangent slope is zero.

The reciprocal derivative is positive at both free positive scales; differentiating 1/φ gives φ′=−ψ′/ψ²<0. For unequal scales the Hessian mixed entry vanishes by equality of the transform values, and the second derivative along (+1,−1) is 2f(0)(φ′(p_i)+φ′(p_j)). At equality the mixed entry is f(0)φ′(p), leaving 2f(0)φ′(p), still negative. The direction stays in the cap box for small steps of either sign.
